answer: Give every identity sole custody of one fragment of a shared relic, encrypted to its key alone. Standing lasts only while it answers unpredictable calls to serve that fragment within a short window. A farm can mint a violet-named clone in seconds, but each clone must then hold and serve a different fragment, forever, on call. When the tide of calls lands on many identities at once, one operator cannot be present as a hundred custodians; missed windows quietly retire the masks. One honest keeper simply answers for its own fragment.
